description: We are Celestial Coders, a team of four Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) students passionate about programming, technology, and space exploration. Our skills include Python, C, C++, Java, React, web development and data analysis. We are developing Project Frontier, a platform that uses NASA data to identify Earth locations similar to Mars and the Moon. Through teamwork, research, and innovation, we aim to apply our CSE knowledge to real-world space exploration challenges.
summary:
Project Frontier is an interactive, data-driven research platform designed to identify and characterize potential terrestrial analogs for Moon and Mars exploration.

Using open NASA and partner-agency datasets, including MODIS, Mars MOLA, Moon LOLA, ESA WorldCover, and Copernicus GLO-30, we analyze Earth environments through land-cover classification, elevation, terrain slope, and spatial-scale comparisons.

Our system identifies 12 Earth research leads and presents three evidence-supported, process-level analog case studies: Sorbas–Gale Crater (sulfate minerals), Tabernas–Jezero Crater (erosion and sediment transport), and Cabo de Gata–Mare Crisium (volcanic landforms).

Through interactive visualizations and transparent scientific analysis, Project Frontier explains both the potential similarities and important differences between Earth and planetary environments. It highlights how terrestrial environments may support planetary research, instrument testing, and future exploration planning.

Our findings represent exploratory research analogies, not certified landing sites or geological equivalence.
details:
Project Frontier — Project Details

1. Project Overview

Project Frontier is an interactive, data-driven planetary analog research platform developed by Team Celestial Coders for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our project addresses the challenge "Identify Earth Locations that Analog the Permanent Moon Base Locations and Mars" by using open Earth, Moon, and Mars datasets to discover, characterize, and investigate terrestrial environments that may support future planetary exploration research.

Rather than relying on visual resemblance alone, Project Frontier combines satellite observations, land-cover information, terrain measurements, and scientific references to investigate potential connections between Earth environments and planetary features.

2. How Project Frontier Works

Our research workflow consists of five major stages:

Data Collection: We use NASA MODIS Earth observations, NASA MOLA Mars terrain data, NASA LOLA lunar elevation data, ESA WorldCover, and Copernicus GLO-30 elevation data.

Data Processing: Python-based processing extracts and validates scientific measurements, including land surface temperature, terrain elevation, slope, and land-cover characteristics. Source integrity checks help maintain traceability and reproducibility.

Earth Location Discovery: Our screening workflow identifies 12 terrestrial research leads within a regional study area in Spain. Candidate screening considers land-cover characteristics, spatial separation, and local terrain conditions.

Planetary Analog Investigation: We examine three documented, process-level Earth–planetary analog cases:

  • Sorbas, Spain ↔ Gale Crater, Mars: Calcium-sulfate-bearing materials and aqueous alteration.
  • Tabernas Desert, Spain ↔ Jezero Crater, Mars: Erosion, sediment transport, and sedimentary feature interpretation.
  • Cabo de Gata, Spain ↔ Mare Crisium, Moon: Volcanic landforms and remote-sensing interpretation.

These regional case studies provide scientific context and are distinct from the 12 terrain-screening research leads.

Interactive Visualization: Our web application presents planetary information, Earth research candidates, terrain measurements, and scientific evidence. The Discovery Lab allows users to examine research findings, compare observations, and understand the limitations of each proposed analogy.

3. Technologies Used

Programming Languages: Python, JavaScript, and TypeScript.

Frontend: React, HTML, CSS, and Vite.

Data Processing: Python scientific and geospatial libraries, including NumPy, PyHDF, and PyProj.

Scientific Data: NASA MODIS, NASA MOLA, NASA LOLA, ESA WorldCover, and Copernicus GLO-30.

Development Approach: Modular data-processing scripts, reproducibility checks, automated validation, and interactive scientific visualization.

4. Innovation and Creativity

Project Frontier connects Earth-based environmental screening with planetary research in a single interactive application.

Our approach combines multiple independent datasets, identifies spatially distinct research leads, evaluates terrain characteristics at different observation scales, and documents scientific uncertainty rather than presenting unsupported similarity scores.

The platform also makes scientific findings more accessible by allowing users to explore evidence and limitations through the Discovery Lab.

5. Scientific Limitations

Earth cannot perfectly reproduce the Moon or Mars. Differences in gravity, atmosphere, radiation, geological history, and observation resolution limit direct comparisons.

Our 12 identified Earth locations are preliminary research leads, not independently validated planetary analog sites. Our three regional case studies demonstrate bounded similarities in materials, geological processes, or landforms, rather than complete geological equivalence.

Project Frontier does not certify landing safety, permanent base suitability, or quantitative Earth–planetary similarity.

6. Intended Impact and Future Applications

Project Frontier aims to support planetary research, scientific education, and the early exploration of potential terrestrial testing environments.

Our findings can help researchers formulate hypotheses, investigate geological and environmental processes, and design future field observations or instrument-testing experiments.

By making open space-agency data more accessible and connecting Earth observations with Moon and Mars research, Project Frontier demonstrates how data-driven exploration can contribute to understanding environments beyond Earth.
